column1: # Python: classes, functions and methods (all listed as functions: a method is a function whose qualified name carries its class), and module-level constants.
# Functions decorated @overload / @typing.overload are signatures, not definitions: they fold into the implementation that follows them, which is one definition starting at the first signature
# (convert_type, K.get). A property getter and its setter stay two definitions; two plain definitions of one name (helper) stay two. Not definitions: imports, calls, base classes.
